Chapter One: Everyday Dismissal — How Women’s Voices Are Undermined.
Picture this: you’re at a party, the room humming with conversation and laughter. Someone starts sharing a story—something they know inside out, maybe something they’ve spent years studying. But before they can even finish their thought, another voice jumps in. Confident, quick to clarify or correct, maybe even friendly about it. But the outcome’s always the same. The original speaker—so often a woman—gets nudged aside, her expertise quietly brushed off.
Sound familiar? This isn’t just about one person talking over another. It’s a pattern that slips into our everyday lives so smoothly, a lot of folks barely notice it. But if you’ve been on the receiving end, you know how it stings. We even have a word for it now: “mansplaining.” That’s when a man jumps in to explain something to a woman—even if she’s the expert in the room. But honestly, that word’s just a crack in the door. Behind it, there’s a whole world of stories where women are talked over, doubted, or simply ignored.
Let me give you an example that really sticks. Imagine a woman who’s spent years writing a book. She’s at a social event, and she mentions her work. Instantly, a man hears the title and starts explaining what the book’s about—to her. He’s maybe read an article or two, and he’s convinced he’s helping. She tries to cut in, but he doesn’t let up. It’s not until someone else finally points out that she’s actually the author that he pauses—just for a second, embarrassed. But you know what? The moment’s gone. And what’s left is that feeling—frustration, disbelief, maybe even resignation.
These moments aren’t rare. They’re everywhere—offices, classrooms, family dinners, you name it. Sometimes the dismissal is so subtle. A raised eyebrow, a patronizing smile, or a gentle suggestion to “let someone else handle it.” Other times, it’s blunt. Maybe a woman shares an idea, nobody reacts. Then a man repeats it, and suddenly it’s brilliant. The message, whether people realize it or not, is loud and clear: women’s voices just don’t carry the same weight.
Most folks don’t even see this happening unless it happens to them. But for those who do experience it, every little dismissal adds up. Each time, it chips away at your confidence. The next time you want to speak up, it’s just a little bit harder. Some women start to wonder—do I really know what I’m talking about? Others just get tired and choose silence, because fighting to be heard is exhausting.
And let’s be honest, this isn’t just about a few awkward conversations. It’s about the way our society is built. From the time we’re kids, boys are told to speak up, to take charge. Girls? They’re taught to be agreeable, to listen, to stay quiet. These lessons stick, shaping not just how we see ourselves, but how we treat each other.
The impact goes far beyond missed ideas or awkward moments. When women’s voices are dismissed, their insights and experiences disappear. Problems don’t get solved, solutions get missed, and whole fields lose out on new perspectives. Sometimes, it gets even more serious. When women try to report harassment or discrimination, their credibility is questioned. People ask for more proof, say maybe they misunderstood, or accuse them of making things up. The habit of not listening to women—that’s a huge roadblock to justice and safety.
But here’s something powerful: naming these patterns makes them real. Once you put a word to it—like “mansplaining”—it’s harder to ignore. People can start pushing back, calling out dismissive behavior, and backing each other up so that everyone gets heard. It’s not everything, but it’s a step. And it’s one we all need if we want a world where every voice truly matters.
